note: Lesson-level recall checks for modules the certification quiz (Appendix B) does not cover. Authored against the lesson text; numbers 1001+ so they never collide with the 100 exam questions, and section 0 keeps them out of the exam paper. Numbers are stable identifiers — the review queue stores them, so renumber nothing.

part-01-l1.q: The guide's five key takeaways name one thing as the real reason enterprises buy Claude Enterprise. What is it?
options: A larger, more capable model than other tiers get
Governance — audit logs, Compliance API, SCIM, spend controls, retention
Exclusive access to Fable 5
A lower per-token price than the API
part-01-l1.why: "Enterprise differentiation is governance, not the model." Competitors run the same models; the control plane is what Enterprise sells.

part-01-l1.q: Which skill does the guide call the highest-leverage advanced skill for both users and admins?
options: Prompt chaining
Fine-tuning
MCP literacy
Writing evals
part-01-l1.why: Connectors are remote MCP servers, and Claude Code and the API consume MCP — so MCP is the connective tissue of the whole platform.

part-01-l1.q: Why does the guide warn that pre-2026 prompting folklore is often counterproductive on 5-series models?
options: The models ignore system prompts entirely
Adaptive thinking replaced manual controls and legacy parameters (budget_tokens, prefill) are deprecated
XML tags are no longer parsed
Few-shot examples now degrade output
part-01-l1.why: The 5-series changed prompting economics: prompt for clear intent and structured context, and let adaptive thinking do the reasoning.

part-04-l1.q: As of August 2026, how is Claude Enterprise priced?
options: $20 per seat per month billed annually, 20-seat minimum, usage billed at API rates on top
$60 per seat per month with usage included
A flat annual platform fee with unlimited usage
$20 per seat per month with a 5-seat minimum and no metered usage
part-04-l1.why: The seat fee buys access and governance; metered usage at API rates is the real variable cost — which is why spend controls exist.

part-04-l1.q: Which capability is available only on sales-assisted Enterprise, not self-serve?
options: SCIM provisioning
Audit logs
A HIPAA BAA
Purchase through AWS Marketplace
part-04-l1.why: Self-serve and sales-assisted share the base seat price, but HIPAA-ready terms (BAA enabled in-app by the Primary Owner) come only with the sales-assisted contract.

part-04-l1.q: Which role is the only one that can enable the Compliance API, accept a HIPAA BAA, and run full data exports?
options: Any Owner
Admin
The Primary Owner (exactly one per org)
Any member of a custom role group
part-04-l1.why: That concentration is why the guide tells you to document who holds Primary Owner and plan succession — an unhandled departure is an operational incident.

part-04-l2.q: What do Enterprise audit logs actually contain?
options: Full chat and file content for the past 180 days
Event metadata only — UUIDs, actor, event, IP, device — for the past 180 days
Conversation titles and summaries, retained indefinitely
Aggregated token counts with no per-user detail
part-04-l2.why: Audit logs answer "who did what, when, from where." Content requires the separate, Primary Owner-gated Compliance API or a data export.

part-04-l2.q: A workspace runs under zero data retention (ZDR). Which of these still works?
options: The Batch API
The Files API
Claude Fable 5
The Messages API
part-04-l2.why: ZDR covers the Messages and Token Counting APIs only. Batch, Files, Skills, code execution and the MCP connector are excluded, and Covered Models (Fable 5, Mythos 5) require 30-day retention.

part-04-l2.q: A customer requires EU data residency. What does the guide say the real procurement decision is?
options: Set the anthropic-client-geo header on claude.ai Enterprise
Claude via AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex EU regions — EU residency is not offered on first-party surfaces
Request an EU workspace from the Anthropic account team
Enable ZDR, which removes the residency question
part-04-l2.why: First-party surfaces default to US infrastructure and offer no EU residency; the EU path runs through the cloud providers under their DPA/BAA.

part-04-l3.q: What is the spend-control difference between self-serve and sales-assisted Enterprise?
options: Both stop automatically when the budget is reached
Self-serve stops org-wide when the prepaid pool hits zero; sales-assisted invoicing has no automatic stop, so limits must be set explicitly
Sales-assisted caps usage at 120% of forecast by default
Neither can set per-user limits
part-04-l3.why: The prepaid pool is a built-in circuit breaker. On invoicing there is none — you can overrun unless you configure limits.

part-04-l3.q: Which cost lever gives a 50% discount but is excluded from ZDR scope?
options: Prompt caching
Model entitlements
The Batch API
User-level spend limits
part-04-l3.why: Route non-urgent API jobs to Batch for half price — but a ZDR workspace cannot use it.

part-04-l3.q: What benchmark does the guide give for Claude Code spend when setting engineering-group limits?
options: Roughly $13 per developer per day
Roughly $13 per developer per month
Roughly $50 per developer per day
Roughly $200 per developer per month
part-04-l3.why: About $13/developer/day is the industry-average burn cited as a useful starting point for group-level limits.

part-08-l1.q: Which plans can use Projects, and what happens when project knowledge outgrows the context window?
options: All plans including Free; extra files are silently dropped
Pro and above; retrieval (RAG) mode expands effective capacity up to ~10×
Enterprise only; the project must be split manually
All paid plans; the oldest files are evicted first
part-08-l1.why: Projects are not on Free. They carry a 200K-token window (500K on Enterprise), and RAG mode kicks in automatically as knowledge approaches the limit.

part-08-l1.q: How does Claude handle PDFs of different lengths?
options: Every PDF gets full vision plus text analysis
≤100 pages: vision + text; 101–1000 pages: text only; over 1000 pages: rejected
≤100 pages: text only; anything longer needs the Files API
PDFs are always converted to plain text before analysis
part-08-l1.why: The 100-page vision cutoff is one of the capability boundaries that trips users far more often than prompting skill does.

part-08-l1.q: What is the default sandbox network posture for code execution?
options: Off everywhere by default
On everywhere with unrestricted internet access
On by default for Free/Pro/Max but limited to approved domains; off by default on Team/Enterprise
On for Team/Enterprise only, since they are the governed tiers
part-08-l1.why: Consumer tiers get approved-domain access (pypi, npm, github, crates.io, Ubuntu archives, api.anthropic.com); the governed tiers start closed.

part-08-l2.q: What is the runtime requirement for a Cowork Scheduled Task?
options: Nothing — it runs in Anthropic's cloud
The computer must be awake with the desktop app open; missed runs re-fire when you reopen it
The mobile app must be installed and signed in
A connector must be marked Always allow
part-08-l2.why: That runtime dependency is the main reason to rebuild a briefing as a cloud Claude Code Routine instead.

part-08-l2.q: What are the documented daily caps on Claude Code Routines (Research Preview, as of August 2026)?
options: Pro 5, Max 15, Team/Enterprise 25 per day
Pro 1, Max 5, Team/Enterprise 10 per day
25 per day on every paid plan
Unlimited, bounded only by spend limits
part-08-l2.why: Research Preview limits change — the guide flags these caps for re-verification before you design around them.

part-08-l2.q: What can the Gmail connector NOT do?
options: Read your mail
Search across threads
Send email on your behalf
Create drafts
part-08-l2.why: Gmail through the connector is draft-only — an example of Layer 3, tool design, bounding what a connector exposes.

part-09-l1.q: The compute/governance gradient says to match each use case against which three variables?
options: Team size, budget, and vendor preference
Task type, context size, and governance needs
Model, plan, and connector count
Latency, accuracy, and cost
part-09-l1.why: Start with low-risk, high-volume workflows, prove value, then escalate to governed, high-context use cases.

part-09-l1.q: What is the hard boundary designers need to know about Claude's visual output?
options: It cannot analyze uploaded images
It cannot render React components
It has no native raster image generation — it produces SVG and code-based visuals only
It cannot produce Mermaid diagrams
part-09-l1.why: Claude analyzes images and generates SVG/HTML/React/Mermaid, but it does not generate photos or bitmap art.

part-09-l1.q: What is Anthropic's recommended hybrid context strategy for Claude Code on a large repo?
options: Paste the whole codebase into the prompt once per session
Anchor with a CLAUDE.md loaded up front, then retrieve everything else just-in-time with glob/grep
Rely entirely on retrieval and skip CLAUDE.md
Keep one long-running session so context accumulates
part-09-l1.why: Standing context up front, everything else pulled on demand — the same principle behind the just-in-time data-analysis pattern.

part-09-l2.q: What does the guide call non-negotiable when reviewing contracts with Claude?
options: Running on Opus 5 rather than Sonnet 5
Quoting the relevant clauses first, then analyzing them
Splitting every contract into 10-page chunks
Disabling connectors during the review
part-09-l2.why: Quote-first grounding is Anthropic's documented anti-hallucination technique for long documents: "Do not summarize clauses you did not quote."

part-09-l2.q: What is the finance-workflow rule of thumb about Claude and arithmetic?
options: Treat all Claude arithmetic as reliable — it uses a calculator internally
Treat arithmetic-through-code as reliable and mental arithmetic as not
Never let Claude near financial figures
Round every figure to avoid precision errors
part-09-l2.why: Ask for the reconciliation logic and totals before trusting output; every figure should arrive with the code that computed it.

part-09-l2.q: How should marketing style guidance be phrased in a prompt?
options: As a long list of prohibitions so nothing goes off-brand
As what Claude should do, anchored by 3–5 diverse exemplar assets
As a single adjective, to leave room for creativity
As a scoring rubric only, with no examples
part-09-l2.why: Tell Claude what TO do; curated few-shot examples steer voice far better than an accumulating laundry list of rules.

part-09-l3.q: Which single instruction does the guide call the highest-value line in support prompting?
options: "Respond in under 100 words."
"Always sound empathetic."
"If the article doesn't cover it, say so and draft an escalation instead of improvising."
"Cite the customer's ticket ID in every reply."
part-09-l3.why: It converts hallucination risk into a clean escalation — the difference between a wrong answer and a routed one.

part-09-l3.q: What should sales teams know about connector write actions in HubSpot?
options: They are logged as system actions with no user attribution
They appear in HubSpot's audit log attributed to the user, so treat them as your own edits
They bypass HubSpot permissions since Claude uses a service account
They cannot be audited at all
part-09-l3.why: The connector also respects your CRM permissions — Claude never sees records you couldn't see yourself — so gate writes behind approval.

part-09-l3.q: What is the consulting-workflow rule about client context?
options: Keep one Project for all clients so patterns transfer
One Project per engagement — never mix client Projects
Store client data in chat scrollback rather than Projects
Publish client artifacts so the team can remix them
part-09-l3.why: Knowledge isolation keeps client contexts separated; publishing client-confidential artifacts is the matching mistake to avoid.

part-10-l1.q: How does the guide distinguish a workflow from an agent?
options: Workflows use tools; agents do not
Workflows orchestrate LLMs through predefined code paths; agents dynamically direct their own process and tool use
Workflows run in the cloud; agents run locally
Workflows are single-model; agents are always multi-model
part-10-l1.why: Anthropic's compact definition of an agent: "LLMs autonomously using tools in a loop."

part-10-l1.q: Which pattern fits a task whose subtasks cannot be predicted in advance?
options: Prompt chaining
Routing
Orchestrator-workers
Parallelization by sectioning
part-10-l1.why: A central LLM breaks the task down at runtime, delegates to workers, and synthesizes — which is literally how Research is built.

part-10-l1.q: What is the opening advice of "Building effective agents" that the guide calls its most important sentence?
options: Always add a verification loop
Prefer orchestrator-workers as the default architecture
Find the simplest solution possible and only add complexity when needed — which might mean not building agentic systems at all
Use the largest model you can afford
part-10-l1.why: Every pattern adds capability and cost, latency, and failure modes. Graduate to one only with a measured reason.

part-10-l2.q: Anthropic's multi-agent research system scored +90.2% over single-agent on its internal eval. What is the matching cost fact?
options: It uses roughly 15× the tokens of ordinary chat
It uses roughly the same tokens, spread across agents
It costs 50% less because subagents run on Haiku
Token usage explains almost none of the performance variance
part-10-l2.why: Agents generally run ~4× chat tokens and multi-agent research ~15×, with token usage explaining 80% of performance variance — so don't spend it on a single-fact lookup.

part-10-l2.q: How should a 20k+ token prompt be ordered?
options: Query first, then documents, so intent frames the reading
Long documents at the top, the query at the end
Alternate document and question blocks
Order does not measurably matter
part-10-l2.why: Anthropic measured up to ~30% quality improvement from putting documents first and the question last.

part-10-l2.q: You have corrected Claude Code three times on the same task and it is still off. What does the guide say to do?
options: Keep correcting — each pass narrows the error
Switch to a larger model and continue in the same session
Clear and restart with a more specific prompt
Add "CRITICAL: You MUST" language to the instruction
part-10-l2.why: Correcting over and over is a documented failure mode; the kitchen-sink session degrades recall as context grows (context rot).

part-10-l3.q: How should screenshots be arranged in a UX-critique prompt?
options: Text first, then images, so the model knows what to look for
Images before text, each labelled (e.g. "Image 1:") so you can reference them
One image per message, never more
Images inline between instruction sentences
part-10-l3.why: Text-before-image ordering produces weaker results; tiny or blurry screenshots are a documented error source.

part-10-l3.q: Which file type is not supported as an input at all?
options: PDF
XLSX (with code execution enabled)
PPTX
CSV
part-10-l3.why: PPTX is an output type only — as are ZIP archives on the input side. XLSX reads reliably but requires code execution.

part-10-l3.q: Writing marketing copy and then translating it in a separate step is an example of which pattern?
options: Prompt chaining — Anthropic's own canonical example
Routing
Evaluator-optimizer
Orchestrator-workers
part-10-l3.why: Generate-then-translate is the canonical chain; use evaluator-optimizer on top when you can score the asset against explicit criteria.

part-10-l4.q: You have legacy code that forces JSON by prefilling the assistant response. What happens on Claude 4.6+?
options: It still works but costs more
It returns a 400 error — migrate to Structured Outputs
It silently degrades to free-form text
It works only when tool_choice is set to any
part-10-l4.why: Prefilled responses are deprecated on 4.6+. Structured Outputs give a structural guarantee rather than a behavioral one.

part-10-l4.q: What is the just-in-time pattern for analyzing a large dataset in Claude Code?
options: Load the full CSV into context so nothing is missed
Write targeted queries, use head/tail and pandas to profile, and store intermediate results to files
Split the file into 200 chunks and paste them sequentially
Ask for estimates rather than computed aggregates
part-10-l4.why: Dumping whole datasets into the prompt causes context rot — and trusting aggregates that were never actually computed is the matching failure.

part-10-l4.q: What does legacy "CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool" language do on current models?
options: Improves tool selection accuracy
Is ignored entirely
Causes over-triggering
Forces a 400 error
part-10-l4.why: Keep tool sets small and unambiguous instead: if a human engineer can't say which tool applies, an agent can't either.

part-14-l1.q: How is API usage billed relative to a Claude Pro or Enterprise subscription?
options: Subscription seats include an API token allowance
API billing is prepaid credits, completely separate from subscriptions
API usage is invoiced against the same seat contract
Enterprise seats grant unlimited API access
part-14-l1.why: A seat license buys you nothing at the API layer — credits are purchased in the Console.

part-14-l1.q: Which header carries an Anthropic API key?
options: Authorization: Bearer
x-api-key
anthropic-version
anthropic-beta
part-14-l1.why: Bearer tokens are reserved for short-lived OAuth / Workload Identity Federation credentials. anthropic-version pins the API contract and must be sent explicitly.

part-14-l1.q: A response contains a tool call with an ID prefixed srvtoolu_. What do you do?
options: Execute it and return a tool_result
Nothing — Anthropic's infrastructure already ran it; never return a tool_result
Retry the request without tools
Return an empty tool_result to acknowledge it
part-14-l1.why: toolu_ means your code must execute and return a result; srvtoolu_ is a server tool that already ran.

part-14-l2.q: What is the classic streaming bug the guide warns about?
options: Deltas can arrive out of order
Errors can arrive mid-stream after the connection already returned HTTP 200
message_start can fire more than once
Thinking blocks are not signed
part-14-l2.why: Status-code-only error handling misses in-stream error events like overloaded_error — always handle the error event itself.

part-14-l2.q: What are the prompt-caching token multipliers, and in what order does invalidation cascade?
options: Read 0.1×, 5-min write 1.25×, 1-hour write 2×; invalidation cascades tools → system → messages
Read 0.5×, write 1×; invalidation cascades messages → system → tools
Read free, write 2×; caches never invalidate within the TTL
Read 0.1×, write 1×; caches are shared across workspaces
part-14-l2.why: Any byte change in a prefix invalidates everything after it, and caches are scoped per workspace. Check usage for cache_read_input_tokens to confirm hits.

part-14-l2.q: What are the per-request PDF limits on the API, and what do you do beyond them?
options: 50 pages / 10 MB; split the document manually
100 pages / 32 MB; upload via the Files API and reference the file_id
1000 pages / 500 MB; no workaround needed
There is no page limit, only a 32 MB size limit
part-14-l2.why: Claude reads both the text layer and page images, so scanned documents and charts come through — within those limits.

part-14-l3.q: What does the Message Batches API trade for its 50% discount?
options: Model quality — batches run on Haiku only
Latency and streaming; results arrive within 24 hours
Tool use, which is unavailable in batches
Prompt caching, which is disabled for batched requests
part-14-l3.why: Ideal for eval sweeps, backfills, and nightly enrichment. Expired requests are not billed, and results are retained 29 days.

part-14-l3.q: You send thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 8000} to Opus 4.7. What happens, and what is the current approach?
options: It works; adaptive thinking is opt-in
The request errors — use thinking: adaptive with output_config.effort instead
The budget is silently ignored and thinking is disabled
It works but thinking tokens are billed as input tokens
part-14-l3.why: Legacy budgets are unsupported on Opus 4.7 and later. Thinking tokens bill as output tokens either way, so effort is your cost/latency dial.

part-14-l3.q: What is the mental model for a 429 versus a 529?
options: 429 is the service's problem; 529 is yours
429 is your problem — slow down and honor the headers; 529 is Anthropic-wide capacity — back off with jitter
Both mean the request is malformed; do not retry
Neither is retryable
part-14-l3.why: Both are retryable, but for different reasons — and 529 can surface inside a 200-OK stream as an error event.

part-14-l4.q: How does the Claude Agent SDK differ from Claude Managed Agents?
options: The Agent SDK runs the agent loop in your process; Managed Agents is a hosted REST service priced per session-hour
They are the same product under two names
The Agent SDK is hosted; Managed Agents runs locally
The Agent SDK is TypeScript-only; Managed Agents is Python-only
part-14-l4.why: A single async query() replaces the manual tool loop and runs the built-in tools — in your process, against your files.

part-14-l4.q: Where do you enforce policy on an Agent SDK run?
options: In the system prompt, by describing the rules
In hooks — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit
In the model choice
In max_tokens, by bounding what the agent can do
part-14-l4.why: Hooks are in-process callbacks with matchers — your enforcement point, and where irreversible actions get gated.

part-16-l1.q: What is the Golden Rule of prompt clarity?
options: Every prompt should fit in 200 words
Show the prompt to a colleague with minimal context — if they would be confused, Claude will be too
Always include at least ten examples
State constraints as prohibitions so nothing is ambiguous
part-16-l1.why: Treat Claude as a brilliant but brand-new employee who lacks your norms and workflow context.

part-16-l1.q: What is the champion model for team adoption?
options: A mandate from leadership with a deadline
One credible practitioner per team who coaches peers by modelling real workflows
A vendor-delivered training day for the whole org
A centre of excellence that reviews every prompt
part-16-l1.why: Adoption spreads through people, not mandates — champions model workflows in shared Projects rather than delivering slide decks.

part-16-l1.q: Audit logs cover the past 180 days. What does that imply operationally?
options: Nothing — Anthropic archives older logs on request
Export on a schedule or stream via the Compliance API; do not discover the limit during an investigation
Retention controls extend audit-log life automatically
You should disable audit logging to save storage
part-16-l1.why: Logs expire; investigations start late. Scheduled export well inside the window is the governance checklist item.

part-16-l2.q: Which pairing of model and price is correct as of August 2026?
options: Haiku 4.5 at $1/$5 per MTok and Opus 5 at $5/$25 per MTok
Haiku 4.5 at $5/$25 and Opus 5 at $1/$5
Sonnet 5 at $10/$50 and Fable 5 at $2/$10
All 5-series models share one price
part-16-l2.why: Fable 5 sits at $10/$50, and Sonnet 5's introductory $2/$10 rises to $3/$15 on 2026-09-01 — verify before quoting.

part-16-l2.q: What token multipliers should you expect from agentic workloads?
options: Agents ~4× chat, multi-agent research ~15×
Agents ~1.5× chat, multi-agent research ~3×
Agents and chat are equivalent; only the model matters
Agents ~15× chat, multi-agent research ~4×
part-16-l2.why: That is why the monthly cost review looks at Claude Code and agentic workflows separately from ordinary chat.

part-16-l2.q: What is the guide's working rule on sharing chats?
options: Share freely; links are unguessable
Never share a chat containing customer data, credentials, personal data, or pre-release information; review the whole thread first and prefer sharing a cleaned artifact
Only Owners may create share links
Publish artifacts instead of chats — published artifacts are always private
part-16-l2.why: Shared and published content propagates further than users expect — links get forwarded and remixes get published.

part-16-l3.q: Why does every shared project need a named knowledge owner?
options: To approve new members
To prune stale documents and resolve contradictions — Claude will try to follow contradictory instructions
To hold the Primary Owner role
To pay for the project's usage
part-16-l3.why: Document hygiene in Projects' RAG is more impactful than prompt tuning, and contradictions must be resolved rather than layered over.

part-16-l3.q: How should each item in Anthropic's monthly release notes be triaged?
options: Communicate, configure, or ignore
Adopt, defer, or reject
Critical, high, or low
Users, admins, or developers
part-16-l3.why: An assigned owner and a monthly review slot turn a monthly release cadence from a surprise into a process.

part-16-l3.q: What does every deprecation or model retirement need attached to it?
options: A changelog link only
A migration owner and a deadline
A vendor support ticket
A spend-limit adjustment
part-16-l3.why: Organizations that skip this get surprised by removals like budget_tokens and prefill.

options: Client, gateway, and provider
Host (the AI app), client (one per server, inside the host), and server (exposing tools, resources, prompts)
Broker, worker, and registry
Agent, subagent, and connector
part-19-l1.why: The protocol splits into a JSON-RPC 2.0 data layer and a swappable transport layer, identical across transports.

part-19-l1.q: When is the stdio transport the right choice over Streamable HTTP?
options: For shared remote servers behind TLS serving many clients
For local filesystem, git, and shell tools with local credentials and exactly one client
Whenever OAuth 2.1 is required
For anything that needs horizontal scaling
part-19-l1.why: stdio launches the server as a local subprocess; Streamable HTTP is the single-endpoint transport for shared remote servers.

part-19-l1.q: What does domain capture do beyond routing logins through your SSO?
options: Deletes personal accounts on your domain
Pulls existing individual accounts on your domain into the managed workspace
Enables SCIM automatically
Grants IP allowlisting
part-19-l1.why: It solves shadow IT — which is why staff should be told before you flip it; their history moves into an org you administer.

part-19-l2.q: How do the four layers of the connector permission stack combine?
options: As a union — any layer that grants access grants it
As an intersection — removing access at any one layer removes it entirely
The Claude-side org policy overrides the other three
OAuth scopes override the source system's permissions
part-19-l2.why: Source-system permissions ∩ OAuth scopes ∩ MCP tool design ∩ Claude-side admin policy = what Claude can actually do.

part-19-l2.q: What distinguishes a subagent inside the agentic loop?
options: It shares the parent's context window to stay in sync
It has its own context window and tool set, attributed back via parent_tool_use_id
It can only run read-only tools
It bypasses hooks
part-19-l2.why: You shape the loop from three directions — configuration (CLAUDE.md, permissionMode), the tool surface, and hooks — and delegate through subagents.

part-19-l2.q: Two governance properties of Projects matter for enterprises. Which pair is correct?
options: Cross-chat search and memory do not leak across project boundaries; sharing is role-based (Private / View / Edit)
Projects are always public to the org; artifacts are private to their creator
Memory is shared across all projects; sharing is all-or-nothing
Project knowledge is encrypted client-side; sharing requires an admin
part-19-l2.why: RAG retrieval assembles only the relevant passages per query, and artifacts are shared only among project members.
